newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb kills four, injures 15 at Kashmir rally.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills four, injures 15 at Kashmir rally.

text.p: A bomb exploded during a political rally on Wednesday in India's troubled Kashmir Valley, killing four people and injuring at least 15, police said.

The device went off in Kulgam town, 65 km (40 miles) south of the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, Srinagar, while the Communist Party of India-Marxist's state leader Yusuf Tarigami was addressing supporters, they said.
Tarigami was elected to Jammu and Kashmir's assembly during polls in September, the first local elections in the Himalayan region since a separatist rebellion erupted in 1990.
One of Tarigami's bodyguards was injured in the explosion, but the politician was not hurt, police said.

Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in the seven-year insurgency. India accuses Pakistan of arming and training guerrillas, but Islamabad says it offers them only moral and diplomatic support.
